claim: Tumor-Treating Fields (TTFields) therapy uses low-intensity alternating electric fields to disrupt microtubules in cancer cells undergoing mitosis.
source: TTFields are low intensity (1–3 V/cm) alternating electric fields applied at frequencies ranging from 100 to 400 kHz (Kirson et al., 2004; Mumblat et al., 2021) and have been shown to impact polar proteins during cellular replication, specifically tubulin.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kirson et al., 2004; Mumblat et al., 2021) and represents established knowledge about TTFields mechanism.

claim: Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) are F-actin-based cellular protrusions that can connect two or more cells at long-range.
source: Tunneling nanotube (TNTs) are cell-contact-dependent filamentous-actin-based cellular protrusions that can connect two or more cells at long-range.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about TNTs based on established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: TNTs are upregulated in cancer and facilitate cell growth, differentiation, and chemoresistant phenotypes.
source: They are upregulated in cancer, facilitating cell growth, differentiation, and in the case of invasive cancer phenotypes, a more chemoresistant phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about TNT function in cancer contexts.

claim: TTFields at 1.0 V/cm significantly suppressed TNT formation in biphasic subtype MPM.
source: TTFields at 1.0 V/cm significantly suppressed TNT formation in biphasic subtype MPM, but not sarcomatoid MPM, independent of effects on cell number.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing TNT suppression in MSTO-211H cells.

claim: TTFields at 1.0 V/cm did not significantly suppress TNT formation in sarcomatoid MPM.
source: TTFields at 1.0 V/cm significantly suppressed TNT formation in biphasic subtype MPM, but not sarcomatoid MPM, independent of effects on cell number.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no significant effect on VAMT cells.

claim: TTFields did not significantly affect function of TNTs assessed by measuring intercellular transport of mitochondrial cargo.
source: TTFields did not significantly affect function of TNTs assessed by measuring intercellular transport of mitochondrial cargo via intact TNTs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on mitochondrial velocity measurements presented in Figure 4B.

claim: TTFields induced upregulation of immuno-oncologic biomarkers in an animal model of MPM.
source: We discovered TTFields induced upregulation of immuno-oncologic biomarkers with simultaneous downregulation of pathways associated with cell hyperproliferation, invasion, and other critical regulators of oncogenic growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data presented in Figure 5 and Table 1.

claim: TTFields induced downregulation of pathways associated with cell hyperproliferation, invasion, and other critical regulators of oncogenic growth.
source: We discovered TTFields induced upregulation of immuno-oncologic biomarkers with simultaneous downregulation of pathways associated with cell hyperproliferation, invasion, and other critical regulators of oncogenic growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial transcriptomic data showing downregulation of genes like TNC, FST, and HGF.

claim: TNTs have the ability to physically bridge cells through a spectrum of intercellular distances ranging from 5–10 μm to 100–500 µm and even longer.
source: TNTs have the ability to physically bridge cells through a spectrum of intercellular distances, with a range of 5–10 μm at extreme short-range to 100–500 µm and even longer (Gousset et al., 2013; Lou et al., 2012; Pasquier et al., 2012; Pasquier et al., 2013; Sartori-Rupp et al., 2019; Tishchenko et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research on TNT characteristics.

claim: TNTs were first characterized in 2004 in PC12 cells derived from rat pheochromocytoma.
source: These ultrafine structures were first characterized in 2004 in PC12 cells, a cell line derived from rat pheochromocytoma (Rustom et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original discovery paper by Rustom et al., 2004.

claim: TNTs are non-adherent to the substratum in cells cultured in vitro.
source: Unlike filopodia and lamellipodia, TNTs are non-adherent to the substratum in cells cultured in vitro (Tishchenko et al., 2020; Rustom et al., 2004; Desir et al., 2018; Dubois et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing TNT characteristics.

claim: TTFields therapy is FDA-approved for patients with glioblastoma and malignant mesothelioma.
source: This technology is currently applied concomitantly with standard-of-care treatment approaches for patients with glioblastoma and mesothelioma, with clinical trials also ongoing in many other forms of metastatic or difficult-to-treat forms of cancer.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about FDA approval status of TTFields.

claim: TTFields can disrupt mitosis in malignant cells through impairment of microtubule polymerization.
source: TTFields can disrupt mitosis in malignant cells due to its ability to interfere with mitotic spindle assembly through impairment of microtubule polymerization (Giladi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Giladi et al., 2015 describing the mechanism of TTFields.

claim: Tubulins are heterodimers with two distinct protein domains creating a dipole.
source: The individual subunits of microtubules, known as tubulins, are heterodimers with two distinct protein domains, in which one has a positive end and one has a negative end, creating a dipole (Marracino et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Marracino et al., 2019 describing tubulin structure.

claim: TTFields application creates a nonuniform electric field during telophase leading to dielectrophoresis.
source: Additionally, TTFields application creates a nonuniform electric field during the telophase phase of mitosis due to alignment of the cell in cytokinesis, leading to a process known as dielectrophoresis, which can also result in improper cell division and mitotic death (Mun et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mun et al., 2018 describing dielectrophoresis mechanism.

claim: Unidirectional TTFields treatment at 200 kHz had fewer TNTs than the control at 24 hr (p=0.004).
source: We found that by 24 hr, unidirectional TTFields treatment at 200 kHz had fewer TNTs than the control (p=0.004) and bidirectional application at 150 kHz (p=0.005).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical significance values provided.

claim: Bidirectional application at 200 kHz had statistically significantly fewer TNTs compared to control (p<0.0001).
source: As compared to control, bidirectional application at 200 kHz also had statistically significantly fewer TNTs (p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data with statistical significance value provided.

claim: Unidirectional application at 150 kHz resulted in no significant differences in TNT formation throughout the 72-hr period.
source: However, unidirectional application at 150 kHz resulted in no significant differences in TNT formation throughout the 72-hr period (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data referenced in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Applying TTFields at 200 kHz unidirectionally is more effective at decreasing TNT formation in MSTO-211H cells.
source: Together the data indicated that applying TTFields at 200 kHz unidirectionally is more effective at decreasing TNT formation in MSTO-211H cells and we utilized this frequency for the rest of our experiments.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing different frequencies and directions.

claim: Bidirectional application of TTFields has shown increased cytotoxicity relative to unidirectional delivery.
source: Previously, bidirectional application of TTFields has shown increased cytotoxicity relative to unidirectional delivery (Kirson et al., 2004)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kirson et al., 2004.

claim: Highest cytotoxicity for MSTO-211H cells was displayed at a frequency of 150 kHz.
source: with highest cytotoxicity for MSTO-211H cells displayed at a frequency of 150 kHz (Mumblat et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mumblat et al., 2021.

claim: A statistically significant difference in TNT formation was noted at 48 hr with MSTO-211H cells (p=0.018).
source: Over the 72 hr treatment period, we noted a statistically significant difference in TNT formation at 48 hr with MSTO-211H cells, but this difference was not present at 72 hr (Figure 1B, p=0.018).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B with statistical significance value.

claim: Cell viability of both control and treatment groups was >95% at all time points.
source: In all cases, cell viability of both control and treatment groups was >95% (Figure 1F and G), demonstrating no induction of cell death in the treated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1F and 1G.

claim: TUNEL assay showed 2.4% and 1.8% mean cell death at 150 kHz.
source: For both TUNEL and NucGreen Dead assays, we noted minimal cell death with 2.4% and 1.8% mean cell death respectively at 150 kHz and 3.2% and 1% mean cell death at 200 kHz when referenced with a negative and positive control (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: An 80% reduction in cell count was noted in the TTFields-treated group when compared to control by the 72–96 hour time point when cells were plated at lower density (p=0.003).
source: In concurrence with others, we noted an 80% reduction in cell count in the TTFields-treated group when compared to control by the 72–96 hour time point (Figure 1—figure supplement 5, p=0.003).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 with statistical significance.

claim: There was no difference between samples treated with or without TTFields in actin polymerization.
source: Surprisingly, there was no difference between samples treated with or without TTFields (Figure 2A and B; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: There was no difference in the amount of actin bundling between TTFields-treated samples and controls.
source: Again, there was no difference in the amount of actin bundling between TTFields-treated samples and controls, indicating that TTFields likely affect TNT formation by other factors in this system (Figure 2C and D; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The average velocity of TNT transport in the control group was 3.59 µm/min.
source: In the control group, the average velocity of TNT transport was 3.59 µm/min.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of cargo velocity.

claim: The average velocity of TNT transport was 3.94 µm/min for cells treated with TTFields delivered unidirectionally at 200 kHz.
source: The average velocity of TNT transport was 3.94 µm/min, 4.07 µm/min, and 3.07 µm/min for cells treated with TTFields delivered unidirectionally at 200 kHz, bidirectionally at 200 kHz, or bidirectionally at 150 kHz, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of cargo velocity.

claim: There were no observable differences in visible cargo velocities moving through TNTs in cells treated with or without TTFields.
source: These findings indicated that there were no observable differences in visible cargo velocities moving through TNTs in cells treated with or without TTFields.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on cargo velocity measurements.

claim: The average velocity of mitochondria in the control group was 3.32 µm/min with a standard deviation of 0.504 um/min.
source: In the control group, we showed that the average velocity of mitochondria was 3.32 µm/min, with a standard deviation of 0.504 um/min, and with TTFields treatment an average velocity of 3.43 µm/min, with a standard deviation of 0.17 µm/min (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: With TTFields treatment, the average velocity of mitochondria was 3.43 µm/min with a standard deviation of 0.17 µm/min.
source: In the control group, we showed that the average velocity of mitochondria was 3.32 µm/min, with a standard deviation of 0.504 um/min, and with TTFields treatment an average velocity of 3.43 µm/min, with a standard deviation of 0.17 µm/min (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There was no observable effect of TTFields on mitochondrial transfer in TNTs at the intensity and frequency that suppressed formation of TNTs.
source: This finding indicated that similar to gondolas, there was no observable effect of TTFields on mitochondrial transfer in TNTs at the intensity and frequency that suppressed formation of TNTs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data on mitochondrial velocity.

claim: 22 of the CTA 1812 genes analyzed were differentially expressed following TTFields treatment.
source: Analysis of gene expression showed that 22 of the CTA 1812 genes analyzed were differentially expressed (Figure 5, Table 1, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data shown in Figure 5 and Table 1.

claim: Application of TTFields results in regulation of genes involved in cell adhesion and motility, PI3K-AKT signaling, and immune response.
source: Broadly we found that the application of TTFields results in regulation of genes involved in cell adhesion and motility, PI3K-AKT signaling, and immune response; and to a lesser extent MAPK and MET signaling, and matrix remodeling-metastasis (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: TNC is a glycoprotein involved in the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
source: TNC is a glycoprotein involved in the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and was previously found by our group to be upregulated in TNT promoting conditions (Ady et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors and represents established knowledge.

claim: TNC expression was 2.5-fold lower in TTFields-treated tumors compared to negative control.
source: TNC expression was 2.5-fold lower in TTFields-treated tumors compared to negative control (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data shown in Table 1.

claim: LYZ is associated with neutrophil degranulation and host defense peptides.
source: LYZ is associated with neutrophil degranulation and host defense peptides
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about LYZ function.

claim: COL1A1, COL1A2, HGF, TNC, and VEGFA are all part of the PI3K pathway.
source: whereas COL1A1, COL1A2 along with HGF, TNC, and VEGFA are all part of the PI3K pathway, which plays an important role in cancer progression, and has been implicated in TNT regulation (Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2011 and represents established pathway knowledge.

claim: CX3CR1 was upregulated in TTFields-treated tumors overall.
source: Expression of immunogenic markers with implications for efficacy of immuno-oncology therapeutic strategies were also found, and included CX3CR1, which was upregulated in TTFields-treated tumors overall, as well as the aforementioned HLA-DRB, C1R and COL3A1.
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data analysis.

claim: VEGFA was notably downregulated following TTFields treatment.
source: Markers of angiogenic activity, such as VEGFA, which are also implicated in EMT, hypoxia signaling pathways and cell adhesion and motility, also were notably downregulated.
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data analysis.

claim: TNTs observed in TTFields-treated tissue measured approximately 4 µm in length.
source: In TTFields-treated tissue, we similarly identified TNTs, or at least TNT-like protrusions, via analysis of a z-stacked 60 x field of view with high Ki-67 expression measuring approximately 4 µm in length (Figure 6C; Figure 6—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: TNTs in intact tumor specimens were markedly shorter than their in vitro counterparts.
source: The TNTs that we visualized ex vivo were markedly shorter than their in vitro counterparts.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison of in vitro and ex vivo imaging data.

claim: Differences in TNT length could be attributed to density of the tissue stroma and sectioning thickness.
source: These differences in length could be attributed to density of the tissue stroma and sectioning thickness, which reduces the likelihood of long-range cell communication via TNTs.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning about why TNTs are shorter in tissue.

claim: Tenascin C is a modulator of cell invasive potential.
source: Using COL1A1, a modulator of mesenchymal invasive potential (Comba et al., 2022) which we found to be upregulated following TTFields treatment (Figure 5B–C), provides support in identifying potential drivers of TTFields treatment resistance.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Comba et al., 2022.

claim: Tenascin C was upregulated in mesothelioma cells primed in cell culture conditions conducive to TNT formation.
source: We have previously reported that Tenascin C, a modulator of cell invasive potential, is upregulated in mesothelioma cells primed in cell culture conditions conducive to TNT formation (Ady et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors (Ady et al., 2014).

claim: Transition of mesothelioma cells to EMT is strongly associated with a sharp rise in TNT formation.
source: Furthermore, transition of mesothelioma cells to EMT is strongly associated with a sharp rise in TNT formation (Lou et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors (Lou et al., 2012).

claim: TNT formation occurred primarily in high Ki-67 expression ROIs.
source: We also observed that TNT formation occurred primarily in high Ki-67 expression ROIs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the imaging data of tumor sections.

claim: There may be a functional association between in vivo TNTs and increased proliferation within the tumor.
source: Although there appears to be less reliance on TNTs for communication within dense stroma, there may be a functional association between in vivo TNTs and increased proliferation within the tumor.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observation of TNTs in high Ki-67 regions.

claim: TTFields added to standard-of-care treatment improved overall survival by 4.9 months in glioblastoma patients.
source: With increasing evidence for the role of TMs in glioblastoma biology, potential effects of TTFields on TMs may account at least in part for the significant improvements in overall survival (4.9 months) when TTFields are added to standard-of-care treatment (Stupp et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Stupp et al., 2017 clinical trial data.

claim: MSTO-211H is a biphasic MPM cell line.
source: MSTO-211H cells are a biphasic MPM cell line that was purchased from the American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, Rockville, MD, USA) for use in this study.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the cell line used in the study.

claim: VAMT is a sarcomatoid MPM cell line.
source: VAMT is a sarcomatoid MPM cell line that was authenticated prior to use using STR profiling.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the cell line used in the study.

claim: 'Thin' (<700 nm) nanotubes contained only actin in MSTO-211H cells.
source: A previous study from our group (Jana et al., 2022) using the same mesothelioma cells (MSTO-211H) reported that co-localization of different cytoskeletal elements revealed a striking difference in the nanotube structure based on geometric width. 'Thin' (<700 nm) nanotubes contained only actin, while both microtubules and vimentin intermediate filaments were localized to 'thick' (>700 nm) nanotubes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors (Jana et al., 2022).

claim: Both microtubules and vimentin intermediate filaments were localized to 'thick' (>700 nm) nanotubes in MSTO-211H cells.
source: A previous study from our group (Jana et al., 2022) using the same mesothelioma cells (MSTO-211H) reported that co-localization of different cytoskeletal elements revealed a striking difference in the nanotube structure based on geometric width. 'Thin' (<700 nm) nanotubes contained only actin, while both microtubules and vimentin intermediate filaments were localized to 'thick' (>700 nm) nanotubes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors (Jana et al., 2022).

claim: MSTO-211H cells formed thin TNTs that did not harbor MTs and showed a lack of tubulin expression when grown in standard culture plate conditions.
source: When grown in standard culture plate conditions, MSTO-211H cells formed thin TNTs that did not harbor MTs and showed a lack of tubulin expression.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the prior study cited and the experimental conditions used.

claim: TTFields may affect TNT formation through activation of the Rho-ROCK pathway and promotion of reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton.
source: Indeed, TTFields application has been shown to activate the Rho-ROCK pathway and promote reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton, which may explain our findings on TNT suppression in MSTO-211H (Voloshin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is speculative, connecting cited work (Voloshin et al., 2020) to the authors' findings.

claim: The maximum suppression of TNT occurring unidirectionally vs bidirectionally may indicate that the orientation of the affected TNT component plays important roles in TNT formation.
source: Indeed, when controlling for other parameters, the maximum suppression of TNT occurring unidirectionally vs bidirectionally may indicate that the orientation of the affected TNT component as well as its identity may play important roles in TNT formation.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the experimental data on directional effects.

claim: TTFields cytotoxic effect in vitro is affected by cell density.
source: However, when MSTO-211H were seeded at a lower density and exposed to TTFields, markedly reduced cell counts were observed at 72–96 hr of exposure, indicating that TTFields cytotoxic effect, at least in vitro, is affected by cell density.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing different cell densities.

claim: MSTO-211H was categorized as sensitive to the cytotoxic effects of TTFields.
source: It was found that of the 30 cell lines tested, MSTO-211H was categorized as sensitive to the cytotoxic effects of TTFields (Giladi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Giladi et al., 2015.

claim: Properties specific to individual cell lines could allow for resistance to TTFields treatment.
source: Such a finding could explain the discrepancy in TNT formation between MSTO-211H and VAMT, suggesting that properties specific to individual cell lines could allow for resistance to TTFields treatment.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the differential response of cell lines.

claim: Upregulation of CSF1, CX3CR1, and HLA-DRB with concurrent modulation of the tumor microenvironment may induce an inflammatory niche susceptible to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
source: Upregulation of factors such as CSF1 (macrophage colony stimulating factor-1, a cytokine responsible for macrophage production and immunoresponse), CX3CR1 (chemokine signaling), and HLA-DRB (lymphocyte trafficking and T cell receptor signaling), with concurrent modulation of the tumor microenvironment (TME) mediated by increased expression of collagens COL1A1, COL1A2, and COL3A1, may induce an inflammatory niche susceptible to cutting edge therapeutic including immune checkpoint inhibitors.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the spatial genomic data.

claim: Spatial genomic analysis suggests a possible role for combining TTFields with immunotherapy and/or selective targeted therapies.
source: Overall, our spatial genomic analysis suggests a possible role for combining TTFields with immunotherapy and/or selective targeted therapies in creating a more drug targeted friendly TME.
evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the spatial genomic data.

claim: TNTs and TNT-like protrusions can be imaged in intact tumors.
source: This work builds on evidence from our team dating back to 2010 demonstrating that TNTs and TNT-like protrusions can be imaged in intact tumors (Lou et al., 2012; Lou et al., 2017; Lou et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work by the authors.

claim: The authors designate their new method as Spatial Profiling of Tunneling nanoTubes (SPOTT).
source: Superimposing these regions of interest from spatial genomics over the plane of TNT clusters imaged in intact tissue is a new method that we designate Spatial Profiling of Tunneling nanoTubes (SPOTT).
evidence: This is a definitional statement about the new method developed by the authors.

claim: These results position TNTs as potential therapeutic targets for TTFields-directed cancer treatment strategies.
source: In sum, these results position TNTs as potential therapeutic targets for TTFields-directed cancer treatment strategies.
evidence: This claim is a speculative conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: TTFields may provide a potential novel strategy for converting tumors from 'cold' to 'hot' for potential response to immunotherapeutic drugs.
source: We also identified the ability of TTFields to remodel the tumor microenvironment landscape at the molecular level, thereby presenting a potential novel strategy for converting tumors at the cellular level from 'cold' to 'hot' for potential response to immunotherapeutic drugs.
evidence: This claim is a speculative conclusion drawn from the spatial genomic data.

claim: A TNT protrusion in heat-treated native tissue was 4.5 µm long in the XY plane at 60X magnification.
source: The one shown in Figure 6 is in the form of a TNT protrusion in a high Ki-67 expressed ROI, 4.5 µm long in the XY plane at 60 X.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Both TNT protrusions were suspended three-dimensionally within the tissue microenvironment of the sample.
source: Analysis of the z-stack at Nyquist sampling using IMARIS 3D revealed an additional TNT protrusion of the same length labeled by Alexa Fluor 647 phalloidin; and both were suspended three-dimensionally within the tissue microenvironment of the sample (Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by 3D microscopy analysis shown in Figure 6—video 1.

claim: The observed protrusions were consistent in appearance with previous results identifying TNTs/TNT-like protrusions connecting cells in intact human tumor specimens from mesothelioma patients.
source: Each of the identified protrusions was consistent in appearance with our previous results identifying TNTs/TNT-like protrusions connecting cells in intact human tumor specimens from mesothelioma patients.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison with prior observations by the authors.

claim: The protrusions were both shorter in comparison to the human version and much shorter in length than the TNTs observed in vitro.
source: The protrusions were both shorter in comparison to the human version, and also much shorter in length than the TNTs we observed in vitro.
evidence: This claim is inferred from comparison of different experimental observations.

claim: Eight total mice were injected with AB1 mesothelioma cells and assessed for tumor growth until they reached 200 mm3 in size.
source: Eight total mice were injected with AB1 mesothelioma cells and assessed for tumor growth until they reached 200 mm3 in size.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the experimental methods.

claim: Four mice each were treated with TTFields using the inovivo device, or heat sham for a negative control.
source: Four mice each were treated with TTFields using the inovivo device, or heat sham for a negative control, as described in Materials and Methods.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the experimental methods.

claim: A total of twelve regions of interest (ROI) were chosen from eight tumors.
source: One section from all eight tumors was adhered to a glass slide, as per Nanostring GeoMx instructions, from which a total of twelve regions of interest (ROI) were chosen.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the experimental methods.

claim: Six ROIs were from TTFields-treated tumors, and six from heat sham-treated tumors.
source: Six ROIs were from TTFields-treated tumors, and six from heat sham-treated tumors.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the experimental methods.

claim: NanoString's GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler system was used to analyze the expression level of 1812 genes within the ROIs.
source: NanoString's GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler system, with their mouse cancer transcriptome atlas (Catalog Number: GMX-RNA-NGS-CTA-4), was used to analyze the expression level of 1812 genes within our ROIs.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the experimental methods.

claim: The genes most prominently affected (downregulated) in TTFields treated tumors were Tenascin C (TNC), FST, and HGF.
source: The genes most prominently affected (downregulated) in TTFields treated tumors as compared to the heat controls, were Tenascin C (TNC), FST, and HGF (Figure 5B and C, Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data shown in Figure 5B, 5C, and Table 1.

claim: Upregulation was most prominent for HLA-DRB, LYZ, COL1A1, and COL1A2.
source: In contrast, upregulation was most prominent for HLA-DRB, LYZ, COL1A1, and COL1A2.
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data analysis.

claim: Cells in low Ki-67 ROIs had a low rate of cell division and were more affected by TTFields application.
source: We reasoned that as the cells in these regions had a low rate of cell division, they were more affected by TTFields application, and thus potentially would be more likely to reveal genes that regulate TNT formation.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning about why low Ki-67 regions were focused on.

claim: COL1A1 is a modulator of mesenchymal invasive potential.
source: Using COL1A1, a modulator of mesenchymal invasive potential (Comba et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Comba et al., 2022.

claim: COL1A1 was upregulated following TTFields treatment.
source: Using COL1A1, a modulator of mesenchymal invasive potential (Comba et al., 2022) which we found to be upregulated following TTFields treatment (Figure 5B–C)
evidence: This claim is supported by spatial genomic data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Tumor microtubes (TMs) have been associated with invasion resistance to treatment with chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery in an animal model of glioblastoma.
source: An analogous cellular protrusion called 'tumor microtubes' (TMs) has been associated with invasion resistance to treatment with chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery in an animal model of glioblastoma (Jung et al., 2017; Osswald et al., 2015; Osswald et al., 2016; Weil et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work on tumor microtubes.
